bubble.$description: The fifth piece of the Message/Bubble/Attachment family — the plain conversational reply, deliberately small scope enforced by the component itself, not just documentation: text (text-style.body-base, reused verbatim) plus at most one Attachment, nothing else. No headings, no images, no CTA slot — those belong to Message, the rich sibling this was split from by content type, not by sender (confirmed against the real screenshots: even a staff member's own short reply is a Bubble, not a Message). Two roles, not a size ladder: 'self' (the current viewer's own message, right-aligned) and 'other' (anyone else's, left-aligned) — same self/other split the staff-mobile mockups already use, and it generalizes correctly to the student-facing desktop app too (there, the student is always 'self'). radius.lg (16px), not radius.default (8px) — deliberately larger, the same 'signals a distinct surface' reasoning Modal/Popover's own bigger radii already use, so a bubble doesn't read as just another ordinary control. Sender avatar/name/timestamp are NOT part of this token file — same composition-not-token-file treatment as MessageThread/FilterPanel in the approved plan; the docs page demonstrates a bubble with its sender row using the exact same Avatar-based pattern Message's own sender row already established, not a second one.

self.$description: The one open call flagged in the plan, resolved the same way Message's own chrome default was: the live desktop app's own reply bubble is a pale tint (not the staff-mobile mockup's solid saturated blue), so tint is the default and solid is documented as the secondary option for whichever surface wants the mockup's stronger look — live product outranks mockup, same precedent Message already set. tint reuses bg.primary+text.default (a light blue wash behind ordinary dark reading text, not colored text — a whole paragraph in text.primary blue would read like a link, not a message). solid reuses fill.primary+text.onFill verbatim, the same pair every other 'solid' surface in this system already uses.

other.$description: One fixed look, not a tint/solid axis — reuses Card's own exact recipe (surface.default + border.default) rather than inventing a lookalike white surface.
